title: bthci: Separate HCI Commands and Events vendor payload table
description:
To untangle the payload table in better support of the Vendor-specific HCI events.
More detailed discussion can be seen in the merge request.

Please provide a sample capture using one of these vendor-specific sub events you would like to dissect this way.

Hi John, thanks for the quick review. Attached a sample btsnoop file and a simple dissector below. This follows a portion of https://source.android.com/docs/core/connect/bluetooth/hci_requirements#bluetooth-quality-report-command

Note that due to some confidential content, the btsnoop file has been greatly truncated and the dissector is very basic for now. But it should be enough. Let me know if more details are needed. Thanks again!

[bqr_sample.log](/uploads/6757b9065999bd33969dab2597f496b8/bqr_sample.log)
[packet-btbqr.c](/uploads/7ea461fc79e38aa503f9a3d86de1019c/packet-btbqr.c)

Thanks. So part of the problem is that the existing `bthci_evt` dissector handling of the Vendor-Specific Events is broken, and apparently always has been.

Those tables are for Vendor-Specific Commands and when called from `dissect_bthci_evt_command_status`, `dissect_bthci_evt_command_complete`, or `dissect_bthci_cmd` (from `bthci_cmd`), those are all situations where the tvb passed in to the vendor dissectors starts with a two-byte opcode whose upper ten bits (OGF) indicate vendor specific handling.

The case there, however, is where the single byte event code is `FF` and there is a Vendor-Specific Event. What needs to be passed to a dissector table has to be two bytes later than what is currently being passed in, after the length. It should most likely be a different table, because those are events, not commands.

It is true that Google uses the single byte after the length as an opcode field. However, at least some vendors do define the next *two* bytes as an opcode field (e.g., TI).

I don't think we can guarantee that all vendors use Google's interpretation.

Got it. Thanks John for taking the time to look into this and the detailed explanation.

For sure if there are other specs using 2 or more bytes as opcode my code right here is not the way to go.

Let's discuss the next steps on the next thread("Vendor-Specific Events should be treated differently than Commands"). I'm resolving this thread.

How did you generate the btsnoop file above? Btsnoop files have a flag for each packet indicating direction. All of your packets, both host to controller and controller to host, indicate the same direction (sent).

The vendor dissectors use the direction to determine whether a packet should be interpreted as an event or command. That's why your file didn't work.

Thanks John for following up after quite some time. I believe I just cherry picked the packets out of a full BTSnoop from one of my android phone. You have a good point on the direction and maybe I messed up the direction in someway.

But after this change, internally we are able to make it work with full BTSnoops from our Android phones. So thanks again!

The problem with this change is that the other vendor dissectors included with Wireshark do not behave like your dissector, so I am afraid this will be changed. There are several places where vendor specific dissection is necessary:

1. In Bluetooth HCI Command packets, which have Vendor specific Command Opcodes
2. In Bluetooth HCI Event packets, with the vendor specific Event Code
3. In Bluetooth HCI Event packets, with Command Status or Command Complete, when the command opcode inside the event is a vendor specific opcode. Note that this is *not* dissected as the Command packet for the opcode, but does depend on both the event and the opcode.

The dissectors inside the Wireshark source tree handle all three cases with one dissector for each vendor. They look at the `pinfo->p2p_dir` and use that to determine whether the packet is a Command or and Event. If it is an Event, they still expect to receive the Event code, not two bytes later (after the parameter length), so that they can handle the Vendor Specific Event, Command Status Event and Command Complete Events all differently.

This change broke handling for those dissectors. While there may be a case for having more tables - note with your method you would need *four tables - or for something like `register_dissector_with_data`, I am afraid it's not acceptable to break dissectors included with Wireshark to accommodate some third party internal dissector.

So this is going to be largely reverted, and you will have to change your internal dissector to the common behavior of the vendor dissectors in the source tree. 

Even if there are separate Event and Command dissectors, the Event dissectors still need to handle three different Event Codes.

Shoot, thanks for the clear explanation and my apologies for my ignorance. Yes, I fully agree with the next steps. We'll adapt our internal dissectors towards the after-reverting version of Wireshark.

Thanks for taking the time on this John.

> Previously, the vendor-spefic events are sent to be dissected based on the chip vendor. 

This is not entirely correct. The first thing that happens is that it is sent to a payload table which ignores the chip vendor and overrides it. By default, that table (described as "BT HCI Vendor" in Decode As) is set to be configured to do nothing, in which case it is dissected based upon the chip vendor.

The first thing that needs to happen is that Vendor-Specific Events should be treated differently than Commands. After that, then you would be able to add your Google specific events to the payload dissector table and configure it, in which case it would always be tried first before the one on the chip.
Got it, I've made the change of this MR to focus on that. Marking this as ready to be review again.
